title: The King Who Lost and Regained His Crown

keywords: tale of the king who lost kingdom
full_text:
A proud King of ancient Persia was overthrown by a foreign invasion and forced to flee his realm, disguised as an impoverished woodcutter. For seven years, he lived in a mountain village, felling timber with his own hands, turning the heavy plow, and sharing the hardships, bitter winters, and heavy exactions endured by the peasantry.

He saw how the poor were cheated of their grain, how corrupt judges ignored the helpless, and how the labor of the humble sustains the splendor of empires.

When the foreign invaders were expelled and the loyal nobles searched the provinces to restore their rightful king, they found him in a charcoal-burner’s hut, wearing a coarse woollen tunic.

They fell upon their knees, offering him the golden diadem of the empire.

The king took the crown, looked upon it with tears of deep wisdom, and said:

'For twenty years I wore this gold as an ornament of pride; but seven years of poverty have taught me that a crown is a heavy yoke of duty placed upon the servant of the people.

I return to the throne not to be served, but to defend every woodcutter, farmer, and orphan in my realm!'

He ruled for thirty years in unparalleled justice, and his reign became the golden age of Persian chronicles.
moral: Adversity and humble exile teach a monarch the true meaning of justice and the struggles of the poor.
